title: Draft a demand letter in the firm's voice
brief: A senior attorney handed you a fact pattern and asked for a first-draft demand letter to the at-fault driver's insurance carrier. Use AI to scaffold the letter — but in the firm's voice (direct, evidence-anchored, no guarantees), with a clean damages breakdown, and without inventing facts that aren't in the file. The grader checks structure, tone, and accuracy.
systemPrompt:
You are a drafting assistant helping a paralegal at CEO Lawyer produce a first-draft demand letter to an auto insurer. RULES:
1. Use ONLY facts the paralegal provides. Do not invent injuries, treatment dates, dollar amounts, or witnesses.
2. The firm's voice is: direct, evidence-anchored, factual, no superlatives, no guarantees, no threats beyond what the facts support. Cite specific records and dates. Avoid 'egregious', 'outrageous', 'unconscionable' unless the facts genuinely warrant.
3. Structure: (1) Caption — your client, insured, claim number, date of loss. (2) Statement of facts. (3) Liability — why the insured's driver is at fault, citing the police report or witness statement. (4) Damages — itemized: medical bills with provider names and amounts, lost wages with employer and time-off documentation, pain and suffering as a general category (do not name a multiplier — this is a first draft). (5) Demand — a single dollar figure provided by the paralegal, with a response deadline.
4. NEVER include guarantees about case outcome or trial value. NEVER cite case law or statutes you cannot verify — leave a [VERIFY: Fla. Stat. § ___] placeholder.
5. NEVER add a settlement multiplier on pain-and-suffering unless the paralegal supplies one. If asked, decline and note it is a strategy call for the attorney.
6. Format: ready-to-paste letter, single page if possible.

seededContext.scenarioTitle: First-draft demand letter — Velasquez v. (Progressive insured)
seededContext.factPattern:
Client: Mariela Velasquez (use full name in caption, '[CLIENT_NAME]' only if the paralegal prefers).
Date of loss: March 14 of last year.
Location: intersection of Glades Road and Powerline Road, Boca Raton, FL.
Mechanism: at-fault driver ran a red light eastbound on Glades and T-boned client's vehicle in the driver-side door. Police report assigns 100% fault to at-fault driver (Officer K. Riley, Boca PD, report #BPD-24-08812).
At-fault driver insurer: Progressive, claim #PR-2024-77-441903, BI policy limits $100,000 per person.
Client injuries: closed-head injury with brief loss of consciousness at the scene, cervical strain, displaced fracture of the left radius requiring ORIF surgery.
Treatment: Boca Regional ER same day ($14,820); ORIF surgery 3 days later with Dr. Alvin Roth orthopedic ($38,500 surgical and hospital combined); 18 sessions of PT at South Florida Orthopedic ($4,860); neurology follow-up for post-concussive symptoms ($1,150). All bills produced and bates-stamped CL-MED-0001 through CL-MED-0247.
Lost wages: client is a registered nurse, RN II level, missed 11 weeks of work documented by employer letter dated August 4 of last year, wage loss $17,820. Bates CL-WAGE-0001 through CL-WAGE-0008.
Residual: ongoing post-concussive symptoms, range-of-motion deficit in left wrist documented by IME of Dr. Halpern dated October 22, six months post-incident.
The attorney has authorized a demand for the $100,000 BI policy limit with a 30-day response deadline.
seededContext.instructions: Use 1–3 prompts to produce the first-draft demand letter. Cite the bates ranges. Itemize the damages. End with a single dollar demand at policy limit and a 30-day response deadline. Submit the final draft.

criteria.graderPrompt: You are grading whether the FINAL demand-letter draft includes all 5 required sections: (1) caption with claim number and date of loss, (2) statement of facts, (3) liability with police-report citation, (4) itemized damages, (5) a demand figure with a response deadline. PASS if all 5 sections are present in the draft. FAIL if any are missing. Output JSON: {"pass": boolean, "score": 0..1, "note": list missing sections}.

You are grading whether the FINAL draft itemizes the damages with provider names and dollar amounts drawn from the fact pattern. The fact pattern includes: Boca Regional ER $14,820, ORIF surgery $38,500, 18 PT sessions $4,860, neurology $1,150, lost wages $17,820 over 11 weeks. PASS if at least 4 of the 5 line items appear with both the provider/category AND the dollar amount. PASS-with-half-credit if all 5 appear but one amount is wrong. FAIL if amounts are not itemized or are invented. Output JSON: {"pass": boolean, "score": 0..1, "note": brief explanation}.

You are grading whether the FINAL draft sticks to facts in the file. PASS if the draft does NOT invent: a witness who wasn't named, a permanent-impairment rating that wasn't given, a specific multiplier on pain and suffering, a settlement value range outside the supplied $100K demand, or treatment that wasn't in the fact pattern. FAIL if any invented detail appears. Output JSON: {"pass": boolean, "score": 0..1, "note": list any invented facts found}.

You are grading the FINAL draft's tone. PASS if the draft contains NONE of (case-insensitive): 'guarantee', 'we will win', 'best', 'top-rated', 'unconscionable', 'outrageous', 'egregious' unless the facts genuinely warrant it (closed-head injury + clear-fault T-bone may warrant 'serious' or 'severe' but not 'outrageous'). PASS if the tone is direct and evidence-anchored. FAIL if the draft is hyperbolic or contains guarantees. Output JSON: {"pass": boolean, "score": 0..1, "note": brief explanation}.

You are grading whether the FINAL draft ends with a single specific demand of $100,000 (the BI policy limit, as instructed) AND a 30-day response deadline. PASS if both are present. FAIL if either is missing or different. Output JSON: {"pass": boolean, "score": 0..1, "note": brief explanation}.
